title: Finite-diagonal hyper-Ext spectral sequence in the bounded-below second argument
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a small ringed site, with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$ and the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Use $D(\mathcal O)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], its standard cohomology and truncations [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $K,L\in D(\mathcal O)$ and integers $r,c$ satisfy $H^j(K)=0$ for $j>r$ and $H^j(L)=0$ for $j<c$. Put $\mathcal Ext^p_{\mathcal O}(K,F)=H^pR\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(K,F[0])$ for a module sheaf $F$ and any integer $p$. There is a spectral sequence of module sheaves [def-sp-spectral-sequence]
$$E_2^{p,q}(L)=\mathcal Ext^p_{\mathcal O}(K,H^qL)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad H^{p+q}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(K,L),$$
with $d_s$ of bidegree $(s,1-s)$. It is natural and additive in morphisms of $L$, including its abutment maps and filtrations. It vanishes outside $p\geq-r$, $q\geq c$. In total degree $n$ its abutment has a finite exhaustive separated filtration [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-convergence] with graded pieces $E_\infty^{p,n-p}$; only $c\leq q\leq n+r$ occur. In particular $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(K,L)$ has cohomology zero below $c-r$. No constructibility, finite Tor amplitude, or cohomological-dimension bound on the site is assumed.

source.place: Tag 015W, lemma-ss-filtered-derived: filtered-derived spectral-sequence method. The stated internal-Hom/Postnikov variant expands the passage from Ext continuity to representable sums in ILO XVII 10.1.1, proof p. 325; it is not a verbatim specialization of the ordinary left-exact-functor statement.

proof.text: Write $T^n(M)=H^nR\mathcal Hom(K,M)$. For every $M$, take a representative $P$ of $K$ and a K-injective representative $I$ of $M$ as in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Applying [lem-pur-rhom-into-kinjective-local] to $P[-n]$ and $I$ identifies $H^n\Gamma(U,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I))$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(K|_U,M|_U[n])$: the signed source-shift identification gives $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P[-n],I)\simeq\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)[n]$, directly from the Hom-complex differential. Exact module sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact] commutes with the kernel, image and quotient defining cohomology. Thus $T^n(M)$ is the sheafification of the presheaf $U\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(K|_U,M|_U[n])$. This identification is additive and natural in $M$ and $U$: the local bijection sends a cocycle $f$ to its derived morphism $Q_U(f)$, so postcomposition and restriction give the same maps on both sides.

source.place: Tag 0A94, lemma-RHom-into-K-injective; Tag 0A95, lemma-RHom-well-defined (its sheafification argument); module sheafification Tag 03EI, sites-modules-lemma-sheafification-exact.

proof.text: If $M\in D^{\ge b}$, exact restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] preserves cohomology, so $K|_U\in D^{\le r}$ and $M|_U[n]\in D^{\ge b-n}$ for every $U$. For $n<b-r$ one has $b-n>r$, hence $\operatorname{Hom}(K|_U,M|_U[n])=0$ by orthogonality of the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category, def-weil-t-structure]. The presheaf in Step 1 is zero, so $T^n(M)=0$. Taking $b=c$ already proves the claimed vanishing below $c-r$; taking $b=0$ gives $\mathcal Ext^p(K,F)=0$ for $p<-r$.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle; standard orthogonality of upper and lower truncations, as recorded in the cited standard t-structure; Tag 0A94 for Step 1.

proof.text: The functors $T^n$ carry a distinguished triangle $A\to B\to C\xrightarrow{w}A[1]$ to a natural long exact sequence. Indeed exact restriction induces a functor on derived categories preserving cone triangles: it commutes with shifts and with the finite direct sums in the cone formula [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Over each $U$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] and rotations and shifts of the restricted triangle. The connecting homomorphism is postcomposition with $w[n]$ followed by the shift identification. This gives an exact sequence of presheaves, and exact module sheafification gives the asserted sequence of the $T^n$ by Step 1. Naturality of these connecting maps follows directly from the last commuting square of a morphism of triangles, $a[1]w=w'c$; hence it also holds after sheafification.

source.place: Tag 0A94, lemma-RHom-into-K-injective; compare Tag 08JC, lemma-RHom-triangulated. Exactness is proved here from local representable Hom, not inferred from the etale-only lem-sf-hom-triangulated.

proof.text: Use the functorial triangles of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] for $L$: $\tau_{\le q-1}L\to\tau_{\le q}L\to H^q(L)[-q]\to(\tau_{\le q-1}L)[1]$. Put $D^{p,q}=T^{p+q}(\tau_{\le q}L)$ and $E^{p,q}=T^{p+q}(H^q(L)[-q])$. Let $\alpha:D^{p,q}\to D^{p-1,q+1}$ be induced by the next inclusion, $g:D^{p,q}\to E^{p,q}$ by the quotient, and $f:E^{p,q}\to D^{p+2,q-1}$ by the boundary. Step 3 gives respectively $\ker\alpha=\operatorname{im}f$, $\ker f=\operatorname{im}g$, $\ker g=\operatorname{im}\alpha$, and zero consecutive composites. Thus this is the exact couple of [def-sp-exact-couple]. Its derived-couple construction [lem-sp-derived-couple-exact] gives pages starting at $E_2=E$, with $d_s$ of bidegree $(s,1-s)$ and $E_{s+1}=\ker d_s/\operatorname{im}d_s$.

source.place: Tags 011Q, definition-exact-couple; 011R, lemma-derived-exact-couple; 011S, definition-spectral-sequence-associated-exact-couple. Use the project E2 indexing and the truncation triangles of derived.tex Tag 08J5.

proof.text: The right-argument shift comparison [lem-pur-derived-internal-hom-shift-right] identifies $E_2^{p,q}=H^{p+q}R\mathcal Hom(K,H^q(L)[-q])$ naturally with $H^pR\mathcal Hom(K,H^q(L)[0])=\mathcal Ext^p(K,H^qL)$. Step 2 makes this zero for $p<-r$; it is zero for $q<c$ because $H^qL=0$. Also $D^{p,q}=0$ for $q<c$: all cohomology of $\tau_{\le q}L$ is zero, so it is the zero derived object. Iterated pages retain these support bounds since they are subquotients.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle; right-argument shift as in sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JA (definition of internal Hom).

proof.text: Reindex the entire exact couple by $\widetilde D^{P,Q}=D^{P-r,Q}$ and $\widetilde E^{P,Q}=E^{P-r,Q}$. All structure-map bidegrees are unchanged; now $\widetilde D=0$ for $Q<c$, and $\widetilde E=0$ unless $P\ge0,Q\ge c$. Apply [thm-sp-half-plane-convergence] with $a=c$. It gives finite exhaustive separated filtrations on $\widetilde A^N=\widetilde D^{0,N}$, whose graded pieces are $\widetilde E_\infty^{P,N-P}$, and stabilization for $s>\max(Q-c+1,P)$. Returning to the original indices, $N=n+r$, $P=p+r$, $Q=q$; the abutment is initially $A_n=T^n(\tau_{\le n+r}L)$. At total degree $n$, the support conditions are $p\ge-r$ and $q\ge c$ with $p+q=n$, hence exactly $c\le q\le n+r$. Stabilization occurs for $s>\max(q-c+1,p+r)$.

source.place: Tags 011T, lemma-spectral-sequence-associated-exact-couple, and 0BDU/0BDV, definition-bounded-ss/lemma-relate-boundedness; the cited project theorem provides the complete half-plane abutment assertion.

proof.text: The initial abutment map $a_n:A_n\to T^n(L)$ is an isomorphism. In the canonical truncation triangle $\tau_{\le n+r}L\to L\to\tau_{\ge n+r+1}L\to$, the last unshifted term has lower cohomological bound $n+r+1$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category, lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle]. By Step 2 its $T^j$ vanish for $j<n+1$, in particular at $j=n-1,n$. The exact sequence of Step 3 therefore reads $0\to A_n\xrightarrow{a_n}T^n(L)\to0$. This also works when $n+r<c$, when $A_n=0$. All $a_n$ are induced by the natural inclusion of the truncation, so these isomorphisms are natural in $L$.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle; Step 2 supplies the necessary tail vanishing without any completeness or cohomological-dimension assumption.

proof.text: Transport the filtration from Step 6 along $a_n$. Explicitly its $p$-th step in the original indexing is $F^pT^n(L)=\operatorname{im}(T^n(\tau_{\le n-p}L)\to T^n(L))$. For $p+r\ge0$, this is precisely the image filtration of [thm-sp-half-plane-convergence] under the preceding reindexing. For $p+r\le0$, $n-p\ge n+r$ and the map from this larger truncation is an isomorphism on $T^n$, by the same tail calculation as Step 7; thus its image is the whole object, as required by that theorem. For $p\ge n-c+1$, the truncation index is $<c$, so the filtration step is zero. Consequently $F^{-r}=T^n(L)$, $F^{n-c+1}=0$, and $F^p/F^{p+1}\simeq E_\infty^{p,n-p}$. This is the finite exhaustive separated convergence of the statement, including degrees with empty support.

source.place: Tags 011T and 012F (lemma-filtered-differential-ss-converges), with the project half-plane theorem; image filtration spelled out after reindexing.

proof.text: For a morphism $u:L\to L'$, functoriality of the truncation triangles [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] and the explicit natural boundary of Step 3 give maps $D(u),E(u)$ commuting with $\alpha,f,g$. Apply [lem-sp-couple-morphism] to the reindexed couples: the page maps commute with differentials and with the abutment filtrations and graded identifications. Conjugating the abutment map by the natural $a_n$ of Step 7 gives exactly $T^n(u)$; the filtration map is its restriction to the displayed images in Step 8. These constructions are additive in $u$. In fact the canonical truncation and cohomology maps are additive by their kernel/quotient formulas, and postcomposition in each local derived Hom is additive. Thus $D(u+v)=D(u)+D(v)$ and $E(u+v)=E(u)+E(v)$ initially. At every derived-couple stage the maps on images, kernels and their quotients are uniquely characterized by commuting with their inclusions or quotient projections; the sum of the maps for $u,v$ satisfies those equations for $u+v$. Induction proves additivity on all pages, stable pages, filtration steps and graded maps. Identity and composition follow from the same uniqueness and the cited couple-morphism theorem. This proves all the asserted naturality and additivity.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q88-aecb38b20 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all nine steps in full against the statements of all 17 cited nodes. Step 1: the local Hom lemma for K-injective targets (lem-pur-rhom-into-kinjective-local) applied to P[-n], plus exact sheafification, gives T^n as a sheafified local derived Hom. Step 2: exact restriction and t-structure orthogonality give the vanishing for n<b-r. Step 3: covariant Hom out of K|_U applied to the restricted triangles gives the long exact sequence, with the explicit boundary w[n] and naturality from a[1]w=w'c. Step 4: the couple D^{p,q}=T^{p+q}(tau<=q L), E^{p,q}=T^{p+q}(H^qL[-q]) has bidegrees (-1,1), (2,-1), (0,0), and the three exactness equations of def-sp-exact-couple match the long exact sequence of the truncation triangle (checked). Step 5: the right-argument shift gives E2=Ext^p(K,H^qL), and D=0 for q<c. Step 6: reindexing by P=p+r and a=c meets the half-plane theorem's hypotheses exactly, and A^N=T^n(tau<=n+r L). Step 7: the tail tau>=n+r+1 has T^{n-1}=T^n=0, so a_n is an isomorphism. Step 8: re-derived F^p=im T^n(tau<=n-p L); F^{-r} is the whole object, F^{n-c+1}=0, and the graded pieces are E_inf^{p,n-p}. Step 9: the couple-morphism lemma plus the uniqueness of maps on subquotients gives naturality and additivity. Tested on K=O[0], K=F[t], K or L zero, and n+r<c (empty abutment, consistent). No duplicates: thm-sp-truncation-e2 needs a left exact functor between hearts, and RHom(K,-) for a complex K is not one; the other candidates are global, coherent, colimit or lisse statements. There are no new nodes and no cycle (closure of 225 nodes). The ten declared tool_uses are generic homological-algebra tools and I accept them. The Stacks tags 015W/0A94/03EI/08J5/011R were checked in the tags file, there is no SGA, and the statement is unchanged and covers the parent's Step 3 use. No fixes.
